title: 1996 AMC 8 Problem 17
statement: Figure \(OPQR\) is a square. Point \(O\) is the origin, and point \(Q\) has coordinates \((2, 2).\) What are the coordinates for \(T\) so that the area of triangle \(PQT\) equals the area of square \(OPQR?\)

solutions.text:
Since \(OPQR\) is a square with \(O = (0, 0)\) and \(Q = (2, 2),\) we have \(P = (2, 0)\) and \(R = (0, 2),\) so the area is \(2^2 = 4.\)

Triangle \(PQT\) has vertical base \(PQ\) of length \(2,\) and \(T = (t, 0)\) lies on the \(x\)-axis. Its area is \(\tfrac12 \cdot 2 \cdot \lvert 2 - t\rvert = \lvert 2 - t\rvert.\) Setting \(\lvert 2 - t\rvert = 4\) gives \(t = -2\) or \(t = 6.\) Only \(t = -2\) appears among the choices, so \(T = (-2, 0).\)

Thus, the correct answer is C .
hints: The square has side \(2,\) so its area is \(4;\) also \(P = (2, 0)\) and the base \(PQ\) is vertical with length \(2\)
If \(T = (t, 0),\) its horizontal distance from line \(PQ\) is \(\lvert 2 - t\rvert\)
